title: Trusted-base authorization for approved-test and trusted-component changes (V4-TODO-014)
goal: For Guard's own development gate, give the V4 base-owned runner a fail-closed, two-step, single-use authorization path for legitimate changes to approved tests and tiered trusted components, protect those components from silent post-merge weakening, record the judge identity in every verdict, and remove hard-coded product versions from tests, as the prerequisite for the V4-TODO-011 ruleset.
acceptanceCriteria: The runner reads a tiered, explicit, base-owned protected set (verdict and certification components plus approved tests) and accepts a changed protected path only when a base-held record for the root Plan binds its exact base and head hashes and the same diff consumes the record.
Authorization pull requests may only add authorization records and their own Plan pair.
Unauthorized, partial, mismatched, unconsumed, candidate-only, contract-widening and self-authorizing changes fail closed in P6 controls, while unprotected product-code changes still pass.
Runner results and the CI artifact manifest carry verdictComponents hashes of the judging base.
P7, P8 and P10 read the expected version from plugin.json.
The bootstrap PR is accepted under O16 with exact-head Linux-complete and Windows-full certification.
On GitHub, an unauthorized approved-test edit fails v4-required and the same edit passes after a merged authorization PR and a consuming trust-change PR.

Records complete V4-TODO-014, extend V4-TODO-011 phase 2 with review of .github/** and docs/plans/authorizations/**, add the consumer-side follow-up item, retire O16 and close O17, without any ruleset, tag or release.
risks: An authorization mechanism that reads candidate data would let a candidate authorize itself.
Protecting too little keeps silent judge changes possible; protecting too much makes routine product work need authorization.
The bootstrap change is judged by the old runner and must be accepted once more under O16.
Workflow self-modification (G3) is only closed by the V4-TODO-011 ruleset, not by the runner.
decisions: Scope is Guard's own development gate; consumer-side counterparts belong to T7 and a separate backlog item.
Protected set is tiered and explicit in base-owned integrations/github/trust-policy.json; product code is not protected.
Authorization records live in docs/plans/authorizations/, validate against a new additive schema, are added only by authorization-boundary PRs and are consumed by deletion in the trust-change diff.
Authorization and trust-change stay in separate root Plans (existing boundary rule).
Verdict component hashes are recorded through an additive optional ci-artifact-manifest property.
Version expectations in P7/P8/P10 come from plugin.json.
No release in this Plan; the next product release carries the change.
